create table if not exists runtime.browser_signal_events (
  event_id text primary key,
  workspace_id text not null,
  actor_id text not null,
  event_type text not null,
  occurred_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  source text not null,
  page jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  signal jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  evidence_state text not null default 'PARTIAL',
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table if not exists runtime.signal_queue_jobs (
  idempotency_key text primary key,
  title text not null,
  origin text not null,
  destination text not null,
  status text not null default 'queued',
  env text not null default 'dev',
  payload jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  evidence_state text not null default 'PARTIAL',
  close_signal boolean not null default false,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  closed_at timestamptz
);

create table if not exists audit.signal_receipts (
  receipt_id text primary key,
  idempotency_key text not null,
  receipt_type text not null,
  classification text not null,
  detail jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

# Deployment

## Browser
Load the extension folder as an unpacked extension in Chrome or Edge. For production, package through the Chrome Web Store or enterprise extension policy.

## Data
Run db/schema.sql in the database project used by the runtime spine.

## Runtime
Configure the queue endpoint in extension settings. The endpoint must accept the queue job contract and write a worker receipt after processing.

## Done
The system is REAL only when capture creates a telemetry event, creates a queue job, worker consumes the job, receipt is written, and dashboard close state updates.
